text:
On one of those afternoons
with no paint but that of my eyes,
I undressed you
and the journey of my hands and lips
filled your whole body with dew.


That world awakened in the afternoon,
with so many episodes without stories,
was silently flag-borne
and followed by peoples of anxieties.


Between your navel and its surroundings
the eyes of my lips smiled
and your hip,
a sphere in two halves,
brightened the moments of agony
in which my life fled toward your life.


We are so present
that the past does not count unless seen.
We are not what is hidden;
we are in the torrent of life.


Your body is the naked thing in me,
all the water running toward your jars.
Your name, your joy…
No one knows them;
not even you alone.

translation.title: On One of Those Afternoons
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish rendering. The erotic journey, water imagery, and paradoxical closing about private knowledge are preserved.
